A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original simulated federated ASR training experiments, WER results, and ablations on LibriSpeech and Common Voice in Section 4 and Appendices H–I.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds model-width and model-depth experiments in Appendix H.7, Table 21, and Figures 23–24.

M1.justification: The CTC transformer training recipe, client SGD, server LAMB, Gaussian privacy mechanism, and uniform/dimension-based per-layer clipping remain unchanged. The additional model sizes are experimental variants; Algorithm 1 is relocated from the appendix into the main text.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate LibriSpeech and Common Voice v13 English, French, and German, retaining the seed-transfer and heterogeneous-client scenarios. The new size study reuses LS-100 pretraining and CV-en training. Other corpora mentioned in v4's dataset-selection footnote are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Tables 8–9 retain their respective LAMB, LARS, Adam, AdaGrad, and SGD comparisons; Table 13 retains FedProx. The global and per-layer clipping comparators also remain. Newly discussed Nguyen et al. (2023a) is not evaluated as a baseline.

E3.justification: The added H.7 study varies width and depth across 114M–510M-parameter models, sets layer drop to 0.1, and reports relative WER degradation from adding DP. These are settings for an additional controlled study; the retained experiments still specify layer drop 0.3 and their original protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix H.7 adds a model-size sensitivity study comparing global and per-layer clipping across narrow, shallow, baseline, wide, and deep models, with corresponding gradient-imbalance diagnostics. Existing seed, cohort, optimizer, heterogeneity, and layer-specific noise analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report gradient/delta means and standard deviations across clients and training steps. The new model-size plots follow that existing practice; no new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: Table 21 adds model-size WERs and relative DP degradation, including deep-model test WERs of 25.7% with global clipping and 26.4% with per-layer clipping. Tables 1 and 17 newly tabulate global-clipping dev/test WERs of 30.7/35.2% at sigma_DP=10^-5. Table 1 also corrects the C=1, zero-noise per-layer row from 15.9/19.1% to 15.7/18.9%, matching the retained appendix values.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, convergence bounds, lemmas, and proofs are retained. v3 Appendix F maps to v4 Appendix E; changed equation numbering and typography do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the first-practical-benchmark claim, the contribution of combining per-layer clipping with adaptive normalization, and the same headline privacy guarantees and 1.3/4.6-percentage-point WER degradation claims under population extrapolation.

C2.justification: New Appendix D.7 explicitly identifies limits involving read speech, monolingual CTC models, labeled audio, and absent external language models. H.7 adds interpretations connecting model size and DP sensitivity to gradient imbalance. Its assertion that per-layer clipping consistently outperforms global clipping conflicts with the deep-model results in Table 21.

D1.justification: H.7 supplies widths, depths, embedding/MLP dimensions, and layer-drop settings for the additional experiments. Appendix B replaces its planned-code-release wording with an open-source statement, aligning it with the repository already linked in v3's abstract; this does not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds Nguyen et al. (2023a), Batch Clipping and Adaptive Layerwise Clipping for Differential Private Stochastic Gradient Descent. It distinguishes that work's public-data gradient statistics from this paper's structural clipping allocation and optimizer-driven adaptation. The remaining positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include moving Algorithm 1 into the main text, adding limitations and model-size subsections, expanding a related-work paragraph, adding a dataset-selection footnote, and revising front matter and citation style.

P2.justification: v4 substantially redesigns the front page, typography, spacing, table sizing, and figure placement. It adds a graphical privacy–utility summary as Figure 1 and the model-size displays in Table 21 and Figures 23–24. Most earlier displays are retained but relocated and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The width/depth study provides useful evidence beyond v3's single model size, and the explicit limitations clarify applicability. These gains are tempered by inconsistencies: H.7 claims consistent per-layer superiority despite the deep-model counterexample, and Figure 1 labels a baseline near 19.1% as central training although Table 1 gives 17.8%. The overall improvement is therefore limited.
